source.title: Motivair MCDU-70 selection table, applied to the RD113 R1 design
source.basis: Selection table supplied as a screenshot; no file hash could be recorded. RD113_4.2 R1 names the MCDU-70 as the CDU for this design, so the unit's published data becomes an acceptance limit for the generated TCS circuit.

status: The first source in this repository that publishes a flow rate, a connection size and an available pump head, so it is the first external check on steps 3 and 6 of the sizing chain.

expected.evidence: MCDU-70 nominal available pump head pressure 38 psi, which is net at the connections. The generated TCS circuit must live inside the head the selected unit actually offers, and nothing internal to the unit is added to that circuit.
MCDU-70 nominal secondary flowrate 991 GPM. The unit's own pumps must deliver the circuit flow; this is a rating, not a target.
expected.adjudication: SHORT by 15.6 percent at the screening duty. The generator's worst case puts both requested outages in one pod, leaving two of four units to carry it, so each must pass 4334 L/min against the 3750 the MCDU-70 is rated for. RD113 allocates across six of eight on one loop instead. Under the generator's own per-pod assumption the selected unit does not suit; that is a genuine finding and is reported as CDU_RATING_EXCEEDED.

expected.evidence: 2500 kW at primary 105.8 F (41.0 C) and secondary 25% PG at 113 F (45.0 C) - RD113's own FWS 40 C and TCS 45 C.
expected.adjudication: Different operating state. The preset carries Max-Q rack power (188 kW), giving 1444 kW per unit with all eight online. RD113 sizes the CDU on Max-P (227 kW) with six of eight active: 64 racks at 227 kW x 0.96 plus the 8 liquid CIN racks is about 14.3 MW over 6 units, roughly 2.4 MW, which is what the 2.5 MW rating covers. Both figures are correct for their own stated state; the generator represents one operating state at a time and this preset represents Max-Q.

expected.evidence: MCDU-70 nominal secondary flowrate 991 GPM, which reproduces the 2500 kW rating at a 10 K rise.
expected.adjudication: Follows the capacity difference above and confirms it independently. The model's all-online secondary flow is 2167 L/min (572 GPM) at Max-Q; scaled to Max-P over six active units it is about 3600 L/min (950 GPM), within 4 percent of the published nominal. The flow and the capacity disagree by the same ratio, which is what a consistent model should do.

expected.evidence: MCDU-70 primary and secondary connections 6 inch, top entry.
expected.adjudication: VELOCITY CRITERION FINDING, not an arithmetic error. At the published 991 GPM a 6 inch stainless Sch10 bore (161.5 mm ID) runs at 3.05 m/s, above this project's 2.7 m/s TCS header cap, so the generator rounds up to 8 inch. Either the 2.7 m/s cap is conservative for a short equipment nozzle, or the vendor connection is sized tighter than the distribution criterion and needs a transition at the unit. This is exactly the question the velocity cap exists to raise; it cannot be settled from the selection table alone.

not_published.note: The table gives the head the unit delivers, not its internal loss on either side. cdu_design_dp_kPa stays a declared project input, and it is still about a quarter of the modelled circuit budget.
RD113_4.2 states 4 C for the MCDU-70; the selection table does not carry approach at all. The preset uses 5 K, from RD113's own 45 C TCS against 40 C FWS.
No minimum controlled flow, rangeability or authority figures, so the valve operating range still cannot be checked against anything.
